stories.head: Trump, Xi and Putin to hold first three-way talks in China
stories.say: Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin will hold their first three-way meeting next week in Shenzhen, China. Nuclear arms and Iran are on the agenda.
stories.stand: The White House says the leaders will meet on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, with nuclear weapons and Iran on the agenda.
body: The White House said on Friday that US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin will hold their first three-way meeting. It will take place on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, China.

CBS News reported the talks are set for Thursday. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov gave the date as 19 November, Anadolu reported. White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales said Trump would discuss reducing nuclear weapons, and a senior US official said he intends to raise Iran.
US officials said Ukraine would not be discussed. A senior official told Reuters, as quoted by Al Jazeera, that no agreement was expected. The New START arms treaty lapsed in February 2026.
Peskov called the meeting extremely significant. Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has voiced concern that a deal on Ukraine could be discussed without Kyiv, Al Jazeera reported.

stories.head: Zelenskyy says US asked if Ukraine would leave Donbas in return for NATO
stories.say: Volodymyr Zelenskyy says American negotiators asked whether Ukraine would pull out of the Donbas if it were allowed to join NATO. He says Kyiv is not ready to give up territory.
stories.stand: Ukraine's president says it is the first time talks have linked NATO membership to giving up territory.
body: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said US negotiators had asked whether Ukraine would withdraw from the Donbas region if it joined NATO, ABC News reported, citing Reuters. It was the first time talks had linked membership to territorial concessions.
Zelenskyy said Kyiv was not ready to concede territory. He said any comprehensive package, including security guarantees, would be put to a national referendum.
He also dismissed a proposal from Vladimir Putin for a local humanitarian ceasefire around Kostiantynivka. Putin has long called Ukrainian NATO membership a red line.
US-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi ended on Wednesday without a breakthrough, but the sides agreed a prisoner exchange of more than 1,000 people.

stories.head: Kremlin says it will not set terms on who represents Europe in peace talks
stories.say: The Kremlin says it will not dictate who speaks for the European Union in Ukraine peace talks, a shift after Moscow had said Europe had no business at the table.
stories.stand: Dmitry Peskov's comments are the first sign Moscow will not oppose European participation in talks on Ukraine.
body: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on Saturday that Russia would not set conditions on who represents the European Union in talks on ending the war in Ukraine, Euronews reported.
Moscow had previously said EU representatives had no business at the talks. Peskov said Russia should first speak to European representatives to see how they could contribute.

US envoy Jared Kushner said on Thursday that Russia had agreed to include Europe in the next round. On Friday, EU leaders agreed Europe would be represented by Britain, France, Germany, Italy, Poland and the EU institutions.

stories.head: Iran says tankers struck mines near the Strait of Hormuz
stories.say: Iran's Revolutionary Guard says two oil tankers hit naval mines and caught fire south of the Strait of Hormuz, accusing them of using an unauthorised route with tracking switched off.
stories.stand: Iran blamed the ships for using a prohibited route; the vessels have not been named.
body: Iran's Revolutionary Guard navy said two oil tankers struck naval mines south of the Strait of Hormuz and caught fire, Anadolu Agency reported on Sunday. It said the ships had their navigation and tracking systems switched off and were using an unauthorised route.
Al Jazeera reported that Iran's navy described a tanker hitting a mine as the fourth such incident in 24 hours. The ships and their flags have not been named.
The UN has urged an end to attacks on shipping in the region, Al Jazeera reported. Separately, the Revolutionary Guard said it shot down a US MQ-1 drone over Qeshm Island.

stories.head: Siege of Yemen's Taiz raises fears of cholera and disease
stories.say: Aid agencies warn that a Houthi siege of Taiz in Yemen has cut nearly 250,000 people off from healthcare, with more than 1,400 diarrhoea and suspected cholera cases in a week.
stories.stand: UN figures show hundreds of thousands cut off from aid and health care since Houthi forces tightened the siege in October.
body: Houthi forces intensified their siege of the Yemeni city of Taiz in early October, cutting the last major supply route into government-held areas, Al Jazeera reported.

The UN humanitarian office OCHA says nearly 250,000 people have lost access to essential healthcare, including more than 186,000 children under five. It recorded more than 1,400 cases of acute diarrhoea and suspected cholera in one week.

The World Food Programme said in October it could not reach more than 600,000 people who depend on aid in Taiz. Human Rights Watch said the siege may amount to using starvation as a method of warfare. The Houthis deny responsibility and blame government forces.

stories.head: Philippine court orders arrest of preacher Apollo Quiboloy for US extradition
stories.say: A Philippine court has issued an arrest warrant for the jailed preacher Apollo Quiboloy, after a petition linked to America's request to extradite him on sex trafficking charges.
stories.stand: The order follows a US extradition request; Quiboloy is already on trial in the Philippines and denies wrongdoing.
body: A court in Makati issued an arrest warrant and a hold-departure order for the preacher Apollo Quiboloy on Thursday, after finding probable cause, Al Jazeera reported, citing AFP.

A Justice Department spokesman said the petition was filed on Monday, three months after the US asked for his extradition in August. A 2021 US indictment accuses him of sex trafficking conspiracy, child sex trafficking and bulk cash smuggling.
Quiboloy is held without bail while on trial in Pasig for human trafficking, and faces a child abuse trial in Quezon City. He has pleaded not guilty.
A presidential press officer denied the timing was linked to President Donald Trump's visit to Manila on 17 November.

stories.head: German MPs give intelligence agencies power to disrupt threats
stories.say: Germany's parliament has passed a law letting its spy agencies actively disrupt threats, such as hacking servers used by state-backed attackers, rather than only gather information.
stories.stand: The Bundestag passed the reform by 308 votes to 190; opponents warn of a German secret police.
body: Germany's Bundestag passed a law on Friday letting its intelligence agencies actively disrupt threats rather than only gather information, Al Jazeera reported. The vote was 308 to 190, with 71 abstentions.

The foreign intelligence service, the BND, will be able to act against threats abroad, including disrupting servers used by state-backed hackers. The domestic service, the BfV, can take technical steps such as deleting stolen data from an attacker's server.

Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt called it a reform of the century. The governing CDU and SPD backed it; the AfD and Die Linke opposed it. Die Linke warned it could create a secret police. The main provisions take effect on 31 December.

stories.head: Thousands protest across Portugal over housing costs
stories.say: Thousands of people marched in dozens of Portuguese cities on Saturday against rising rents and a government bill that would speed up evictions and remove rent caps.
stories.stand: Protesters want rent caps and more public housing; the government says its bill will increase supply.
body: Thousands of people joined protests in dozens of Portuguese cities on Saturday over rising housing costs and stagnant incomes, Euronews reported. Anadolu Agency put the number of cities at 32.

Protesters demanded rent caps, stronger tenant protection and more public housing. They oppose a government bill that would speed up evictions and remove rent caps. The government argues the bill will increase the supply of rental homes.
EU data show house prices relative to incomes rose by 60.8% between 2015 and 2025. The government says rents have risen 68% since 2020 and has pledged 145,000 new homes.

stories.head: France sees a fifth straight Saturday of nationwide protests
stories.say: Protesters marched across France for a fifth Saturday in a row, over living costs, schools and a police bill. The interior ministry counted about 106,000 people.
stories.stand: Turnout estimates differ sharply, and unions have called another strike for Tuesday.
body: Thousands protested across France on Saturday, the fifth consecutive Saturday of nationwide demonstrations, Euronews reported. Yellow Vest activists, students and education unions marched over the cost of living, school funding and a new police bill.
The interior ministry estimated about 106,000 protesters nationwide, including 24,000 in Paris. Organisers claimed 200,000.

Unions have called another strike for Tuesday, rejecting a government offer to raise the minimum wage by 0.6%. A vote on the police bill, which would give officers extra protection when firing weapons on duty, is expected next week.

stories.head: Southeast Asian leaders meet in Manila ahead of Trump's visit
stories.say: Southeast Asian leaders gather in Manila from Sunday for their summit, where President Trump will meet the Philippines' Ferdinand Marcos on Tuesday before heading to China.
stories.stand: US tariffs hang over the ASEAN summit; American imports from the bloc rose sharply last year.
body: Leaders of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations meet in Manila from Sunday to Tuesday, Al Jazeera reported. US President Donald Trump meets Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr on Tuesday before travelling to the APEC summit in Shenzhen.
Trump's administration announced duties of 10 to 12.5 percent on many trade partners in July, after the US Supreme Court struck down his earlier 'reciprocal' tariffs in February.
US figures show imports from ASEAN rose more than 29% to $453.6bn in 2025. Leaders may sign a Digital Economy Framework Agreement during the summit.

stories.head: Drone attacks on cargo ships in the Black Sea leave sailors missing
stories.say: Drone attacks on cargo ships in Bulgarian and Romanian waters have left 11 crew missing from one vessel, with at least 38 people killed in the Black Sea since June.
stories.stand: Bulgarian rescuers describe weeks of attacks; analysts expect more, and NATO has sent patrol aircraft.
body: Drones have hit a string of cargo ships in the western Black Sea, ABC News reported from Varna, Bulgaria. On 13 October a drone blew a hole in the Malta-flagged Chelsea 3 about 40 km from Varna; all aboard were rescued.
The Guinea-Bissau-flagged HS Dignity was hit by several drones. Five crew were rescued and 11 are missing.

At least 38 people have been killed since June, ABC reported. In October nine cargo ships were hit in Bulgarian and Romanian economic zones. A former Bulgarian defence minister said Russia aims to cut Ukraine's sea trade. NATO has sent patrol planes and radar systems to the region.

stories.head: US airlines clear backlog after Friday's nationwide ground stop
stories.say: American airlines are clearing a backlog after Friday's five-hour nationwide ground stop. Officials blame overloaded, ageing equipment in air traffic control.
stories.stand: Officials blame ageing air traffic equipment; airlines warn it could take days to return to normal.
body: US airlines were working through a backlog on Saturday after a nationwide ground stop on Friday, ABC News reported. The stop on departures lasted about five hours and was lifted at 8:15pm Eastern Time.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said ageing routers became overloaded with data, causing inconsistencies in the system. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there was no evidence of a cyber attack.

Federal Aviation Administration chief Bryan Bedford said airlines expected to cancel 4,000 to 5,000 of about 41,000 scheduled flights, Anadolu Agency reported. Airlines for America expects nearly 29 million passengers over Thanksgiving, from 20 to 30 November.

stories.say: Joao Franco of Below Deck and his brother have been arrested in Bodrum, Turkey, after a fight that left a seventeen-year-old dead. They say they acted in self-defence.
stories.stand: The brothers told police they were attacked and denied hitting the teenager.
body: Joao Franco, a yacht captain who appeared on Bravo's Below Deck spinoffs, and his brother Carlos were formally arrested in Bodrum, Turkey, after a fight that left a 17-year-old dead, CBS News reported, citing AP and local media.
According to the Demiroren News Agency, the brothers got into an argument with shopkeepers last Saturday evening. The teenager fell and hit his head, and died in hospital on Monday.
The brothers, both Portuguese nationals, told police they were attacked and acted in self-defence. They denied hitting him. Reports did not specify charges.

stories.stand: Detectives are reviewing several allegations; Walliams says he is not a sexual predator.
body: The Metropolitan Police has launched an investigation into the author and comedian David Walliams over alleged sexual offences, ITV News reported on Friday.

The Met said it had received several allegations of non-recent serious sexual offences involving a man now in his 50s and was reviewing recent reports. It has not said how many offences were reported or when they allegedly happened.
Walliams denies the allegations and any criminal activity. He said he was devastated that some women he met 10 to 20 years ago had expressed hurt or anger towards him.

stories.say: The US Air Force responded to suspected unauthorised drone activity over RAF Lakenheath in Suffolk on Friday. The base says nothing and no one was affected.
stories.stand: The Ministry of Defence says the incident is resolved and it is still establishing the facts.
body: US Air Force security forces responded to suspected unauthorised drone activity over RAF Lakenheath in Suffolk on Friday, ITV News reported.
A base spokesperson said no personnel, aircraft or infrastructure were affected. The Ministry of Defence said the situation was resolved and it was still establishing the facts.

The local MP, Nick Timothy, said he had been told there was no threat to the public. The base declared a heightened alert in September, and US aircraft were moved from nearby RAF Mildenhall earlier this week.

stories.say: A senior US Army officer based in Gloucestershire has been arrested by counter-terror police on suspicion of helping a Russian intelligence service. The Kremlin denies any link.
stories.stand: He is being held under the National Security Act; police can detain him until Tuesday.
body: Counter-terror police arrested a senior US Army officer near Gloucester on Tuesday on suspicion of spying for Russia, ITV News reported. The US military later named him.

He was reportedly based at Imjin Barracks in Innsworth, home to the headquarters of NATO's Allied Rapid Reaction Corps. He is suspected of offences under the National Security Act 2023, covering obtaining or disclosing protected information and assisting a foreign intelligence service.
A warrant of further detention allows him to be held until Tuesday 17 November. He has not been charged. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the arrest did not concern Russia.

stories.head: Government's 'Be Ready' campaign asks households to manage for 72 hours
stories.say: The government's Be Ready campaign is asking households in England and Wales to be able to cope alone for seventy-two hours if power, water or phones fail.
stories.stand: A Cabinet Office survey found only 13% of households felt largely prepared; critics say many cannot afford a reserve.
body: The Cabinet Office's Be Ready campaign asks households in England and Wales to be able to manage on their own for 72 hours if power, water, phone and internet services fail, Al Jazeera reported.
Launched on 22 October, it is a three-year public information effort. Its checklist includes bottled water, long-life food, a torch, a battery or wind-up radio, cash and medication.

In a Cabinet Office survey, only 13% of respondents said their household was largely or totally prepared. More than 180 experts signed an open letter warning that 29% of Britons cannot afford a three-day food reserve.

stories.head: Children will no longer have to declare criminal records under plans
stories.say: Children in England and Wales would no longer have to declare criminal records to employers or colleges under Ministry of Justice plans now out for consultation.
stories.stand: The Youth Justice Board welcomed the proposals, which it says will help rehabilitation.
body: The Ministry of Justice has announced that children will no longer have to declare criminal records to employers and education providers, and has opened a consultation on the reform.
The Youth Justice Board for England and Wales, which has long campaigned for the change, welcomed it. Its chief executive, Stephanie Roberts-Bibby, said children are not little adults.
The board says continued disclosure of childhood records limits access to education and work, which can hinder rehabilitation. It says the reform keeps safeguards for victims and communities.

stories.stand: The government says it has delivered 3,300 new places and aims for 14,000 by 2031.

stories.head: Inquest finds A13 crash deaths might have been avoided after police went to wrong site
stories.say: An inquest jury has found a crash that killed three people on the A13 in east London might have been avoided if police had been sent to the right junction.
stories.stand: A call handler failed to record the correct location of an earlier crash; the Met has changed its training.
body: An inquest jury at Walthamstow coroner's court found that a collision which killed three people on the A13 at Rainham in July 2024 could have been avoided, ITV News reported.

A passing driver twice gave the correct junction for an earlier crash, but the call handler did not record it and officers searched the wrong site. The jury found the fatal crash might have been prevented if police had arrived in time to clear the earlier one.
The coroner, Nina Persaud, raised concerns. The Metropolitan Police said it acknowledged the seriousness of the recording error and has added What3Words to its call handler training.

stories.head: Guernsey parish protests at plan to put most new homes in the north
stories.say: Parish officials in Guernsey are opposing a development plan that would put around fourteen hundred new homes, more than half the island's total, in the north.
stories.stand: The St Sampsons Douzaine says roads, drainage and power have not been properly considered.
body: Parish officials in St Sampsons and the Vale in Guernsey are protesting against the latest Island Development Plan, ITV News reported.
The plan would put 53.7% of the island's new housing in the north, about 1,400 homes, including six affordable housing sites and the regeneration of Leale's Yard.

The St Sampsons Douzaine says planners have not fully considered the strain on roads, drainage, water and electricity, and has suggested other sites. ITV News asked the planning authority for comment.

The call comes from a woman, now 37, who has waived her anonymity and alleges Russell Brand raped her when she was 16 and he was 30. The Metropolitan Police says its investigation into that allegation, opened in January 2026, is ongoing.

First Secretary of State Louise Haigh said the change would be a massive step but deserved proper consideration and scrutiny. Brand is serving a 10.5-year sentence for one rape and three sexual assaults.

stories.head: Driver who fled to Latvia jailed for killing Coventry schoolboy
stories.say: A driver who was doing more than seventy-five miles an hour in a thirty zone when he killed a schoolboy in Coventry, then fled to Latvia, has been jailed for nine years and four months.
stories.stand: Aleksanders Dolars, 23, admitted causing death by dangerous driving and was extradited in August.
body: Aleksanders Dolars, 23, has been jailed for nine years and four months at Warwick Crown Court for causing death by dangerous driving, ITV News reported. He pleaded guilty.

He was driving at more than 75mph in a 30mph zone on Radford Road in Coventry on 14 June 2024 when he hit a schoolboy walking home. He did not stop and fled to Latvia, and was extradited to the UK in August 2026.
He was also banned from driving for 10 years after his release, and must serve two-thirds of the sentence before release on licence.

stories.head: Guaranteed jobs for young people on Universal Credit to roll out across Britain
stories.say: Young people on Universal Credit who have been out of work for a long time will be offered a funded six-month job, under a scheme expanding across Britain from late November.
stories.stand: The government aims to help more than 90,000 18 to 24-year-olds into work by March 2029.
body: The Department for Work and Pensions says its Jobs Guarantee will expand across England, Scotland and Wales from late November, after a trial in six areas.

Eligible 18 to 24-year-olds claiming Universal Credit will be offered a six-month job, with the government paying up to 25 hours a week at the minimum wage. From April 2027, eligibility opens after 12 months out of work, down from 18.

The government aims to help more than 90,000 young people into work by March 2029. More than 400 employers have signed up, and Biffa says it will offer 2,000 roles. Work and Pensions Secretary Pat McFadden said no young person should be left waiting on a scrapheap.

body: Democrat Mary Peltola leads Republican Senator Dan Sullivan in Alaska's Senate race by 49.9% to 46%, Alaska Public Media reported on Saturday. The Associated Press has not called the race.

stories.stand: Scrutiny of AI chip export controls has grown since Nvidia's chief executive resigned.
body: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has agreed to testify before the Senate Banking Committee on 10 December, a US official told CBS News.

Scrutiny has focused on the Commerce Department's apparent delay in adding Singapore-based Megaspeed International to its Entity List. The US government suspects Megaspeed of directing advanced Nvidia chips to China. Megaspeed denies wrongdoing.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told CNBC on Friday that other departments had favoured listing Megaspeed for months, but that Commerce has the pen. The Commerce Department did not immediately comment.

body: Tánaiste Simon Harris wrote on Saturday to political leaders on both sides of the border seeking their views on Irish unity, ITV News reported.

body: A LucidTalk poll for Queen's University Belfast found 52% of people in Northern Ireland support the UK rejoining the EU, with 38% opposed, ITV News reported.
Only 45% see the Windsor Framework as a good thing, its lowest level since June 2021. 63% said Brexit had been more disruptive than expected.

The weighted sample of 1,050 respondents was surveyed from 23 to 26 October. Support for rejoining was highest among SDLP, Sinn Féin and Alliance voters; opposition was highest among TUV and DUP voters.

Polling for the review found 46% of Welsh adults would consider voting Labour again, but only 12% said they definitely would. It recommends a clearer relationship with UK Labour and earlier candidate selection.

stories.say: Nvidia has lost more than five hundred and fifty billion dollars in value in a week since reports about Jensen Huang, a fall felt by many savers in index funds.
stories.stand: Nvidia makes up about 6% of the S&P 500, so the slide reaches many index-fund investors.
body: Nvidia's market value has fallen by more than $550 billion since 6 November, about 13% in one week, CBS News reported. The shares fell after reports about co-founder Jensen Huang's relationship with a suspected Chinese spy, and again when he resigned as chief executive.
Nvidia makes up about 6% of the S&P 500, the index's second-largest company after Apple. CBS said about 97% of US retirement plans offer index funds.

Associate Professor Diego Garcia-Bellido led the work with the South Australian Museum. The area is part of a UNESCO World Heritage bid.

stories.stand: The award, equivalent to an MBE, is the UK's highest honour for a voluntary group.
body: Two hundred and fifty volunteer-led groups have received the King's Award for Voluntary Service, announced on Saturday, the King's birthday.
